archetype.name: Rebuilding Year (defense still missing)
archetype.definition: A second straight bottom-tier season for Utah, a few wins better than 17-65. The offense improved, but the defense stayed among the league's worst, so the year produced some building blocks and no real competitiveness.

report.headline: Five more wins, a better offense, and a defense that got worse

recap.finish: 22-60; last in the Northwest, missed the postseason
recap.body:
Utah went 22-60, and the record is an honest one. W vs Pt Diff was -1 and the margin implied 23 wins, so close games neither saved nor sank them. A Net Rtg of -8.2 ranked 27th, a small step up from last year's -9.2 and 17-65. This was a fast team, with a Pace of 102.3 against a league average of 99.4. That speed explains why 117.59 points a game ranked 9th while the offensive rating ranked only 22nd. More possessions made the scoring look better than it was and made the defense look worse.

The season had one stretch of real hope. After a 2-3 October and a 4-10 November, December went 6-7 with 124.46 points a game, and Utah reached the new year at 12-20. January then went 3-14, and every month after it was a losing one. The longest winning streak all year was two games and the longest losing streak was ten. The finish was the low point. Utah lost nine of its last ten, gave up 132.8 points a game over that stretch, and its only win was a 147-101 rout of Memphis.

The offense is where the progress showed. ORtg rose from 111.2 to 114.1 and TOV % fell from 14.9 to 13.2. Keyonte George carried a 27.9 USG % at 60.9 TS % and scored 1275 points. Brice Sensabaugh added 1116 points at 59.0 TS %. Lauri Markkanen was the best player on the floor whenever he played. He ranked 9th of 93 on the forward tab with a +9.4 On-Off, but he appeared in only 42 games. Jaren Jackson Jr. was also a positive at +5.7 On-Off across 48 games. The frontcourt graded C+ and produced 10.6 Win Shares among its listed players, the only group that carried weight.

The defense undid everything else. Utah's DRtg of 122.3 ranked 29th, worse than last year's 120.4. Opponents posted a 57.8 eFG %, last in the league, and Utah allowed 126.01 points a game, also last. The leaks were on the perimeter. Shooting guards scored 33.93 points a game against Utah, the most any defense allowed, and took a bigger share of opponents' points than the league norm. That fits a backcourt graded D and a wing group graded F. Ace Bailey played the most minutes on the wing with a -4.4 BPM and -0.1 Win Shares. Cody Williams logged 1631 minutes at -5.5 BPM.

This is the third straight season with a defense ranked 29th or 30th, so the problem is structural rather than a bad year. The offense gained real ground. The record barely moved because the other end gave the gains back.

highlights.title: Offense climbed out of the basement
highlights.body: ORtg rose from 111.2 to 114.1 and turnovers dropped sharply from last season. George and Sensabaugh both scored efficiently on heavy usage. Because this came from shooting and ball security rather than close-game luck, it should mostly carry over.

highlights.title: Markkanen and Jackson swung games
highlights.body: Utah was far better with Markkanen on the floor, and Jackson was clearly positive too. They are the reason the frontcourt graded C+ while the other groups sank. The catch is availability: they played 42 and 48 games.

highlights.title: Filipowski was a steady presence
highlights.body: Kyle Filipowski played 77 games and grabbed 552 rebounds. His 3.1 Win Shares and positive On-Off came from a durable, solid contributor rather than a star.

lowlights.title: A defense that got worse
lowlights.body: DRtg slipped to 122.3 and opponents shot a league-worst eFG %. Utah was last in points allowed a game, and the perimeter was the weakest spot, with shooting guards feasting. After three straight years at or near the bottom, this is the core problem.

lowlights.title: Wings graded F
lowlights.body: The wing group combined for 2.1 Win Shares. Ace Bailey took the most minutes there and graded below replacement by Win Shares. Sensabaugh's scoring did not make up for what the group gave away on both ends.

lowlights.title: Collapse after December
lowlights.body: Utah was 12-20 at the turn of the year, then went 3-14 in January and never had a winning month again. It ended 1-9 while allowing 132.8 points a game over that stretch.

arc.note: A December that was close to .500 put Utah at 12-20. From January on it lost steadily and closed by dropping nine of its last ten.

recap.nextYear: No luck needs correcting: W vs Pt Diff was -1, so 22 wins is about what this team was. The offensive gains look durable. They rest on George's and Sensabaugh's efficient volume and on fewer turnovers. Markkanen and Jackson were clearly the team's best two-way pieces, but they played only about half the schedule each. The defense is the priority: it ranked 29th and was worst in the league at stopping guards and wings. The F wing grade and D backcourt grade mark exactly where it breaks down. Unless those perimeter groups improve defensively, a better offense will keep producing records only a little better than this one.
